items.title: Where do locals eat in Koh Samui?

expanded_element.title: Eat Like a Local: Koh Samui Street Food & Hidden Gems
expanded_element.description: Quick Answer: Locals in Koh Samui primarily eat at neighborhood 'Khao Gaeng' (rice and curry) shops in areas like Mae Nam, authentic night markets such as the Nathon night food market, and family-run roadside stalls away from the main tourist beaches. These spots offer genuine Southern Thai flavors at local prices.

expanded_element.title: Is Koh Samui Expensive? A Comprehensive Cost Analysis
expanded_element.description:
Food and dining costs
 Street Food: Fine dining in Koh Samui, especially at beachfront restaurants can cost between 1,500 to 3,000 THB per meal. Street food at night markets can be super cheap with dishes like Pad Thai or Som Tum for 50 to 100 THB. Try Thai Food: Eat local Thai food which is yummy and super cheap.

Drink only bottled or filtered water — including when brushing teeth.
Avoid ice unless you're confident it's from filtered water.
Eat at busy restaurants with high turnover of food.
Be cautious with raw seafood and buffets left in the heat.
